title: Heat exhaustion versus heat stroke
text: Heat exhaustion is heavy sweating, cold or clammy pale skin, weakness, dizziness, headache, nausea, and a fast weak pulse. The person is still sweating and still makes sense when they talk. Move them to shade, loosen clothing, cool them with water and airflow, and give water to sip if they are fully conscious. Heat stroke is a medical emergency: body temperature is very high, the skin is often hot and dry or the person has stopped sweating, and there is confusion, slurred speech, fainting, seizures, or unconsciousness. Call the local emergency number at once, move the person to shade, and cool them aggressively with water while help is on the way.
source: US CDC NIOSH Heat Stress guidance; WHO 2018; OSHA Technical Manual, Heat Stress
